subject.title: iOS/macOS app cannot connect to a Gateway behind a Basic-auth reverse proxy

question: Should macOS adopt the existing per-gateway custom-header contract for both foreground and node Gateway connections, and what secure-store/reset behavior should own those credentials?
rationale: The transport seam exists after the iOS fix, but macOS would introduce credential-bearing settings and storage on a separate app surface, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary alone.

options.title: Approve macOS parity on the existing contract
options.body: Reuse GatewayCustomHeaders with macOS secure per-gateway storage, TLS-only delivery, reset behavior, and tests/proof for both foreground and node Gateway connections.

options.title: Limit macOS to typed Basic/Bearer fields
options.body: Add a narrower macOS proxy-auth UI instead of arbitrary headers, reducing flexibility but tightening the credential surface.

options.title: Defer macOS proxy credentials
options.body: Document macOS authenticated reverse proxies as unsupported for now and keep operators on VPN, SSH tunnel, Tailscale, or proxy-bypass alternatives.

recommendation.title: Approve macOS parity on the existing contract
recommendation.body: Reuse GatewayCustomHeaders with macOS secure per-gateway storage, TLS-only delivery, reset behavior, and tests/proof for both foreground and node Gateway connections.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the merged iOS contract and explicitly marked this issue as the macOS parity tracker.
